title: Digital Assets and Blockchain: A Policy Programme for Government
summary: An eight-module programme giving policymakers the understanding to set digital asset policy, design legislation and meet international standards on crypto-assets and stablecoins.
intro: This training programme equips ministries, legislators and public agencies to understand digital assets and blockchain, weigh their opportunities and risks, and design proportionate legislation, regulatory strategy and international positions.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give policymakers a clear, hype-free understanding of the technology, markets and risks behind crypto-assets, stablecoins and tokenisation, and the regulatory approaches countries have taken. Participants leave able to set a national policy stance, frame legislation and perimeter decisions, ask the right questions of regulators and industry, and meet international commitments from the FSB, IOSCO and FATF.
sections.What It Covers: Blockchain and distributed ledger technology, the crypto-asset market and its participants, risks to consumers, markets and financial stability, regulatory approaches and international standards, stablecoins and monetary sovereignty, tokenisation of real-world assets, innovation hubs and sandboxes, financial crime and the travel rule, and legislative design.
Intended Audience: Officials in finance ministries and treasuries developing digital asset, fintech and innovation policy
Legislative drafters, legal advisers and parliamentary committee staff working on digital asset legislation
Staff of investment promotion agencies, innovation offices and other public bodies engaging with the digital asset sector
Learning Objectives: Explain blockchain, crypto-assets, stablecoins and tokenisation in plain language
Assess the consumer, market integrity, financial crime and stability risks of digital assets
Compare regulatory approaches and the international standards that apply to them
Evaluate the policy implications of stablecoins and tokenised finance for the national system
Weigh the benefits and risks of innovation hubs, sandboxes and investment promotion
Design the core elements of a digital asset legislative and policy framework
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as an intensive programme over two to three days or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a plain-language briefing with case studies and policy options analysis, ending in a legislative design workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the government's priorities.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some familiarity with financial services policy is helpful. No technical background in blockchain or computing is required.
Core Reading: FSB (2023), Global Regulatory Framework for Crypto-Asset Activities
FSB (2023), High-level Recommendations for the Regulation, Supervision and Oversight of Global Stablecoin Arrangements
IOSCO (2023), Policy Recommendations for Crypto and Digital Asset Markets
FATF (2021), Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers
OECD (2022), Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework and Amendments to the Common Reporting Standard

modules.title: Blockchain and Digital Assets Explained
modules.summary: Plain-language grounding in how distributed ledgers, cryptography, wallets and smart contracts work, and the main types of digital asset they support.
objectives: Explain how distributed ledgers and consensus mechanisms work
Distinguish payment tokens, utility tokens, security tokens, stablecoins and NFTs
Separate genuine use cases from marketing claims
syllabus: Distributed ledgers, consensus, keys and wallets
Public and permissioned blockchains and smart contracts
A taxonomy of digital assets for policymakers
The vocabulary officials need: DeFi, staking, bridges, oracles and layer 2

modules.title: The Crypto-Asset Market and Its Risks
modules.summary: How the crypto-asset market is structured, who the main participants are, and the consumer, market integrity and financial stability risks revealed by recent market failures.
objectives: Describe exchanges, brokers, custodians, issuers and DeFi protocols
Explain the risks of conflicts of interest, commingling and market manipulation
Assess the links between crypto-asset markets and the wider financial system
syllabus: Market structure: centralised platforms, vertical integration and DeFi
Consumer harm: fraud, mis-selling, custody losses and platform failures
Case studies of exchange and lender collapses
Financial stability: interconnectedness and spillover channels

modules.title: Regulatory Approaches and International Standards
modules.summary: The policy choices countries have made, from prohibition to bespoke regimes, and the international recommendations from the FSB, IOSCO, BCBS and FATF that shape national frameworks.
objectives: Compare prohibition, existing-law, bespoke and hybrid regulatory approaches
Explain the international standards and the peer review of their implementation
Identify the gaps and arbitrage risks created by divergent national regimes
syllabus: Same activity, same risk, same regulation: principle and practice
FSB global framework and IOSCO policy recommendations for crypto-assets
Prudential treatment of bank crypto exposures
Regional crypto-asset regimes compared: licensing, conduct and market abuse

modules.title: Stablecoins, Monetary Sovereignty and Payments
modules.summary: Why stablecoins matter to government, the risks they pose to monetary sovereignty, payments and financial stability, and the policy options for issuance, reserves and redemption.
objectives: Explain how fiat-backed, asset-backed and algorithmic stablecoins work
Assess the implications for monetary policy, capital flows and payment systems
Evaluate policy options for reserve, redemption and issuer requirements
syllabus: Stablecoin designs and lessons from de-pegging events
Currency substitution and monetary sovereignty in smaller economies
Reserve quality, redemption rights and issuer authorisation
Stablecoins, tokenised deposits and central bank digital currencies

modules.title: Tokenisation and the Future of Financial Markets
modules.summary: How tokenisation of securities, funds and real-world assets could change market infrastructure, and what legal and regulatory changes government may need to make to enable it safely.
objectives: Explain tokenisation and its potential benefits for issuance, settlement and access
Identify the legal certainty issues for ownership, settlement finality and insolvency
Assess the policy case for pilot regimes and legislative change
syllabus: Tokenised bonds, funds and real-world assets
Distributed ledger market infrastructure and settlement assets
Legal foundations: property law, finality and custody
Pilot regimes, sandboxes and public sector issuance

modules.title: Innovation Hubs, Sandboxes and Investment Promotion
modules.summary: How governments attract digital asset business without compromising standards, the design of innovation hubs and sandboxes, and the reputational risks of competing on light-touch regulation.
objectives: Distinguish innovation hubs, regulatory sandboxes and accelerator programmes
Evaluate the economic case and the reputational risks of attracting digital asset firms
Define the respective roles of ministries, promotion agencies and regulators
syllabus: Innovation hub and sandbox design: eligibility, safeguards and exit
Attracting firms: licensing speed, standards and the race to the bottom
Case studies of financial centre strategies and their consequences
Protecting regulatory independence in investment promotion

modules.title: Financial Crime, Sanctions and Tax
modules.summary: The money laundering, terrorist financing, sanctions and tax evasion risks of digital assets, and the government's responsibilities under FATF standards and international tax transparency frameworks.
objectives: Explain how digital assets are used for money laundering, fraud and sanctions evasion
Describe FATF requirements for virtual assets and service providers, including the travel rule
Identify tax reporting and information exchange obligations
syllabus: Typologies: mixers, privacy coins, scams and ransomware
FATF Recommendation 15, VASP registration and the travel rule
Blockchain analytics and law enforcement capability
The OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework and tax policy choices

modules.title: Designing Digital Asset Legislation and Policy
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by examining how to define the perimeter, structure a licensing regime, allocate powers between authorities and plan implementation for a national digital asset framework.
objectives: Define the regulatory perimeter and key legal definitions
Design licensing, conduct, custody and market abuse provisions and allocate supervisory powers
Produce a national digital asset policy and legislative action plan
syllabus: Perimeter, definitions and technology neutrality
Licensing, prudential, custody, conduct and market abuse provisions
Transitional arrangements, enforcement powers and supervisory capacity
Workshop: a national digital asset policy and legislative roadmap

related.title: Payments, Digital Money and CBDCs: Policy for Government
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping policymakers understand payments and digital money and make informed choices on legislation, stablecoins, CBDCs and cross-border payments.

related.title: Crypto-Asset Financial Crime: Typologies, Tracing and Controls
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping supervisors, FIU analysts and investigators to recognise crypto-asset crime typologies, trace funds on-chain and assess service providers' controls.

related.title: AI in Financial Services: Policy Choices for Government
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping policymakers understand AI in financial services and make informed choices on regulation, institutional roles and national strategy.

related.title: Building a Competitive Financial Centre: Strategy, Regulation and Investment Promotion
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping ministries and investment promotion agencies build a competitive, reputable financial centre and measure the results.

related.title: Developing Capital Markets and Investment Fund Industries
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping policymakers develop deep, well-regulated capital markets and fund industries through credible, well-sequenced reform.

related.title: Drafting Financial Services Legislation
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping legislative drafters and legal advisers design and draft effective, enforceable and technology-neutral financial services legislation.
